html:
The Duchy of Benevento was the southernmost state of the Lombards in Italy, centred on the city of Benevento, inland from Naples. Lombard dukes ruled it from 571, soon after their invasion of Italy.

Cut off from the Lombard kingdom in the north by Byzantine and papal lands, it always went its own way. When the Franks conquered the Lombard kingdom in 774, Benevento survived. Its duke took the title prince and held out against Charlemagne. The other Lombard duchies of the south were its neighbours, and in 849 the principality split, with Salerno breaking away.

In the 1000s Norman adventurers carved up the south in the Norman conquest of southern Italy, led by men like Robert Guiscard. The city of Benevento passed to the Papal States, and the last prince died in 1077. The map still draws it to 1200, though by then the land around belonged to the Norman Kingdom of Sicily.
